company.product: Audit-prep workspace for lean finance teams

stages.name: Hit X: first audit passed on the workspace

caseStudies.name: The first-audit controller

pull.project: Get through the company's first financial audit on time, so the sponsor, the lender or the next raise gets the audited numbers it is waiting on.
unavoidable: Sponsor deadline: the PE sponsor set a date for audited financials.
Lender covenant: the credit agreement requires audited statements by a fixed date.
Fundraise or sale: the data room needs audited numbers before it opens.
Unknown, inferred from behavior: they bought and loaded the auditors' list in the first week.
options: Outside help (big-four advisory, temps): too expensive or too slow to start, and they don't know the business.
Doing it in house (spreadsheets, shared drives): can't show auditors a clean trail in time.
pull.limitations: Every option leaves the controller as the bottleneck for every auditor request.

caseStudies.note: All of them face a first audit with a small finance team and a date someone else set. What differs is who set the date: the sponsor, the lender, or a raise.
caseStudies.supply: A workspace that turns the auditors' request list into owned tasks, with evidence attached and a live status the auditors can see.
caseStudies.unblockedLife: Fieldwork starts on time, auditors self-serve evidence, and the controller stops being the bottleneck for every request.
caseStudies.pricing: $40k a year, priced against one advisory engagement, signed before fieldwork starts.
caseStudies.extremeProfile: Controller or VP Finance at a PE-backed company, 50 to 300 employees, first audit with fieldwork under 90 days out, finance team of three or fewer.
caseStudies.whoToTarget: Portfolio companies acquired by PE in the last 12 months; ask sponsors' operating partners for intros.

sections.title: Who we target and why
sections.body: Controllers at PE-backed companies facing their first audit within 90 days. The sponsor's deadline makes the project unavoidable, and the alternatives are too slow or too expensive, so it would be weird for them not to buy.

sections.title: How we reach them
sections.body: Referrals from PE operating partners and LinkedIn to controllers at recently acquired companies. Outreach sells the conversation, not the product: one line about their audit date and a question.

sections.title: How a deal moves
sections.body: Call 1 finds the PULL (the audit date and the request list). Conceptual fit is a walkthrough on their own list. Detailed fit is their auditor's questions. Project planning works backward from fieldwork. Sign before fieldwork.

sections.title: How customers succeed
sections.body: X is passing the first audit on the workspace. Onboarding loads the request list in the kickoff call and gets the auditors logged in during week one.

sections.title: Pricing
sections.body: $40k a year, anchored to one advisory engagement, signed before fieldwork.

sections.title: Current bottleneck and the bet
sections.body: Most first meetings have no audit on the calendar, and a third of selling hours sit empty. The bet: fill those hours with operating-partner intros and PE CFO events, where meetings already pull. Stop booking anyone without an audit date.

coaching.headline: Most of your first meetings have no audit on the calendar. That is the whole problem.
coaching.move: Retarget. The order I want: first, controllers at PE-backed companies with fieldwork under 90 days out. Then anyone with an audit date this year. Nobody else gets a meeting. Your referral meetings already pull at over 60%. Cold email meetings almost never do, and those deals almost never close. It would be weird for a controller with fieldwork in 60 days to ignore you.
coaching.today: Before your 11:00, message the three operating partners who sent you your last extreme-PULL customers. Say: "[Customer] got through their first audit on time with us. Who else in your portfolio has fieldwork this quarter? Two intros would be huge."
ladder: DM 30 controllers at companies PE bought in the last 12 months. One question: when does fieldwork start?
Still stuck? Go to the PE CFO events this month and work the floor.
Still stuck? Ask your current customers' sponsors to send one intro email to the whole portfolio.
coaching.why: Targeting beats every sales fix you could make. PULL deals close at many times the rate of everything else, faster, with a fraction of the seller hours. And a third of your selling hours are empty. Fill them with the same people.
